q: Which definition of software is used in the lecture?
o: Source code and the hardware it runs on
vi: Software = chương trình + tài liệu đi kèm (requirements, design models, user manuals).
en: Software = computer programs plus associated documentation such as requirements, design models and user manuals.

q: Software developed for a single customer according to their specification is called:
vi: Custom: cho một khách theo spec của họ. Generic: bán cho nhiều khách.
en: Custom software is built for one customer to their spec; generic software is sold to a range of customers.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the four attributes of good software in the lecture?
vi: 4 thuộc tính: Maintainability, Dependability/Reliability, Efficiency, Acceptability. Scalability không nằm trong danh sách.
en: The four attributes are Maintainability, Dependability/Reliability, Efficiency and Acceptability. Scalability is not listed.

q: "Software must evolve to meet changing needs" describes which attribute?
vi: Maintainability: phần mềm phải tiến hoá được theo nhu cầu thay đổi.
en: Maintainability: software must evolve to meet changing needs.

q: According to the lecture, Acceptability means software must be:
o: Understandable, usable and compatible with other systems
vi: Acceptability: được người dùng chấp nhận; dễ hiểu, dễ dùng, tương thích với hệ thống khác.
en: Acceptability: accepted by its users; understandable, usable and compatible with other systems.

q: Roughly how are software engineering costs split between development and testing?
vi: Khoảng 60% chi phí là development, 40% là testing.
en: Roughly 60% of costs are development costs and 40% are testing costs.

q: For systems with a long life, which statement about costs is correct?
o: Development always costs more than maintenance
Maintenance costs may be several times development costs
vi: Với hệ thống sống lâu, chi phí bảo trì có thể gấp nhiều lần chi phí phát triển.
en: For long-lived systems, maintenance costs may be several times development costs.

q: According to the CHAOS Report 2020 shown in the lecture, what percentage of IT projects were successful?
vi: CHAOS 2020: 35% thành công, 46% challenged, 19% thất bại.
en: CHAOS 2020: 35% successful, 46% challenged, 19% failed.

q: In the CHAOS Report 2020, the largest group of IT projects was:
vi: Challenged chiếm 46%, lớn nhất.
en: Challenged projects were the largest group at 46%.

q: Which statement best contrasts software engineering with computer science?
o: SE is concerned with theory and fundamentals
SE is concerned with the practicalities of developing and delivering useful software
SE covers hardware, software and process engineering
SE and CS are the same discipline
vi: CS: lý thuyết, nền tảng. SE: thực tiễn phát triển và bàn giao phần mềm hữu ích.
en: CS is about theory and fundamentals; SE is about the practicalities of developing and delivering useful software.

q: Which discipline is concerned with all aspects of computer-based systems development, including hardware, software and process engineering?
vi: System engineering bao trùm HW + SW + process; SE là một phần trong đó.
en: System engineering covers hardware, software and process engineering; SE is the part concerned with software.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the goals of software engineering listed in the lecture?
vi: Mục tiêu: cost effective, on time, high quality, đáp ứng nhu cầu khách hàng. "Công nghệ mới nhất" không có.
en: Goals: cost effective, on time, high quality, satisfying customer's needs. Latest technology is not one of them.

q: Which is NOT one of the four generic activities in software processes?
vi: 4 hoạt động: Specification, Development, Validation, Evolution. Deployment là bẫy.
en: The four activities are Specification, Development, Validation and Evolution. Deployment is the trap.

q: The process activity "checking that the software is what the customer wants" is:
vi: Validation: kiểm tra phần mềm có đúng là thứ khách hàng muốn.
en: Validation checks that the software is what the customer wants.

q: Which process model perspective shows "who does what"?
vi: Workflow: trình tự hoạt động. Data-flow: luồng thông tin. Role/action: ai làm gì.
en: Workflow = sequence of activities; data-flow = information flow; role/action = who does what.

q: Which of the following is listed in lecture 01 as a generic process model?
vi: Generic process models: Waterfall, Iterative development, Component-based SE.
en: Generic process models: Waterfall, Iterative development, Component-based software engineering.

q: Continuous Integration (CI) means:
o: Automatically and frequently integrating code changes
Deploying to production once per release
Merging all branches at the end of the project
vi: CI: tích hợp thay đổi code tự động và thường xuyên. CD: tự động build, test, sẵn sàng release.
en: CI = automatically and frequently integrating code changes. CD = automatically built, tested and prepared for release.

q: According to the lecture, DevOps is:
o: Cultural philosophies, practices and tools that shorten the software development lifecycle
vi: DevOps = Development + Operations: văn hoá, practices, công cụ để rút ngắn SDLC.
en: DevOps = Development + Operations: cultural philosophies, practices and tools to shorten the SDLC.

q: With agentic AI in software engineering, which statement matches the lecture?
o: Engineers are no longer accountable for code written by agents
Clear requirements and good tests matter less
Engineers remain accountable for quality, security and ethics
Agents remove the need for code review
vi: Kỹ sư gõ ít hơn, đặc tả/review/kiểm chứng nhiều hơn, và vẫn chịu trách nhiệm về chất lượng, bảo mật, đạo đức.
en: Less typing, more specifying, reviewing and verifying; engineers remain accountable for quality, security and ethics.

q: "Engineers should not knowingly accept work which is beyond their competence" belongs to which professional responsibility issue?
vi: Competence: không nói quá năng lực, không nhận việc vượt năng lực.
en: Competence: do not misrepresent your competence or knowingly accept work beyond it.

q: Which ACM/IEEE Code of Ethics principle requires lifelong learning about the practice of the profession?
vi: SELF: học tập suốt đời và thúc đẩy cách hành nghề có đạo đức.
en: SELF: participate in lifelong learning and promote an ethical approach to practice.

q: "Software engineers shall maintain integrity and independence in their professional judgment" is the principle:
vi: JUDGMENT: giữ sự chính trực và độc lập trong phán đoán chuyên môn.
en: JUDGMENT: maintain integrity and independence in professional judgment.

q: How many principles does the ACM/IEEE Software Engineering Code of Ethics have?
vi: 8 nguyên tắc: Public, Client & Employer, Product, Judgment, Management, Profession, Colleagues, Self.
en: Eight: Public, Client and Employer, Product, Judgment, Management, Profession, Colleagues, Self.

q: Which statement about ethical behavior matches the lecture?
o: Ethical behavior means simply upholding the law
Ethical behavior is more than simply upholding the law
Ethics is replaced by technical skill
vi: Hành xử đạo đức là hơn cả việc tuân thủ pháp luật.
en: Ethical behavior is more than simply upholding the law.

q: Which abbreviation is expanded CORRECTLY?
vi: SDLC = Software Development Life Cycle · CI = Continuous Integration · CD = Continuous Delivery/Deployment · DevOps = Development + Operations.
en: SDLC = Software Development Life Cycle · CI = Continuous Integration · CD = Continuous Delivery/Deployment · DevOps = Development + Operations.

q: Which characteristic belongs to plan-driven approaches?
vi: Plan-driven: lập kế hoạch trước, đo theo kế hoạch, dựa vào tài liệu, process nặng. Agile: tacit knowledge, process nhẹ.
en: Plan-driven: planned activities, progress measured against the plan, document-based, heavy. Agile: tacit knowledge, light.

q: According to the lecture, the Incremental model is classified as:
vi: Plan-driven: Waterfall, Incremental, Spiral, RUP. Agile: XP, Scrum, Kanban.
en: Plan-driven: Waterfall, Incremental, Spiral, RUP. Agile: XP, Scrum, Kanban.

q: Which of the following is listed as an agile method in the lecture?
vi: Agile methods: Extreme Programming, Scrum, Kanban.
en: Agile methods: Extreme Programming, Scrum, Kanban.

q: Which CMMI maturity level is "Defined"?
vi: 1 Initial → 2 Managed → 3 Defined → 4 Quantitatively Managed → 5 Optimizing.
en: 1 Initial → 2 Managed → 3 Defined → 4 Quantitatively Managed → 5 Optimizing.

q: At CMMI maturity level 2 (Managed), processes are managed at the:
vi: Level 2 Managed: quản lý ở mức project (planned, performed, measured, controlled). Level 3 mới chuẩn hoá toàn tổ chức.
en: Level 2 Managed: managed on the project level. Organization-wide standards come at Level 3.

q: "The organization is data-driven with quantitative performance improvement objectives" describes CMMI level:
vi: Level 4 Quantitatively Managed: đo lường và kiểm soát, data-driven.
en: Level 4 Quantitatively Managed: measured and controlled, data-driven.

q: Which statement about CMMI is correct according to the lecture?
o: It is maintained by the Scrum Alliance
It was developed by SEI at CMU and is now maintained by the CMMI Institute (ISACA); current version V3.0 (2023)
It applies only to hardware projects
vi: CMMI: SEI (CMU) phát triển, nay do CMMI Institute (ISACA) duy trì, phiên bản V3.0 (2023).
en: CMMI was developed by CMU's SEI and is now maintained by the CMMI Institute (ISACA); current version V3.0 (2023).

q: In the waterfall model, development is not started until:
vi: Waterfall: chưa baseline requirements thì chưa bắt đầu development.
en: Waterfall: development is not started when requirements are not baselined.

q: Which statement about the waterfall model in the lecture is FALSE?
o: Two stages cannot be performed at the same time
Each stage must be completed before doing the next stage
Going back to a previous stage is impossible
A stage is completed if a set of criteria is met
vi: Slide ghi rõ: có thể quay lại stage trước (going back is possible).
en: The slide states that going back to the previous stage is possible.

q: The waterfall model is only appropriate when:
vi: Waterfall chỉ hợp khi requirements đã hiểu rõ và ít thay đổi.
en: Waterfall is only appropriate when the requirements are well-understood and changes are limited.

q: In the waterfall diagram, which stage comes right after "Analysis and Design"?
vi: Requirements definition → Analysis and Design → Implementation and Unit Testing → Integration and System Testing → Operation and Maintenance.
en: Requirements definition → Analysis and Design → Implementation and Unit Testing → Integration and System Testing → Operation and Maintenance.

q: In the incremental model, which requirements are developed in early increments?
vi: Requirements được ưu tiên; ưu tiên cao nhất làm ở increment đầu.
en: Requirements are prioritized; the highest priority ones are developed in early increments.

q: Which is a PROBLEM of the incremental model?
o: Lower risk of overall project failure
Highest priority requirements receive most testing
vi: Nhược điểm: process không visible, cấu trúc hệ thống dễ xuống cấp. Ba lựa chọn còn lại là ưu điểm.
en: Problems: the process is not visible and system structure tends to degrade. The other options are benefits.

q: In the spiral model, each spiral (loop) represents:
vi: Mỗi vòng xoắn là một phase; không có phase cố định như specification hay design.
en: Each spiral represents a phase in the process; there are no fixed phases such as specification or design.

q: In the spiral model diagram, "Risk Reduction / Prototyping" belongs to which quadrant?
vi: Plan: requirements gathering. Risk Analysis: risk reduction, prototyping. Engineering: coding, testing. Evaluate: customer evolution.
en: Plan: requirements gathering. Risk Analysis: risk reduction, prototyping. Engineering: coding, testing. Evaluate: customer evolution.

q: Which is a PROBLEM of the spiral model?
vi: Nhược điểm: phức tạp, đắt, phụ thuộc nhiều vào risk analysis, khó quản lý thời gian.
en: Problems: complex and expensive, too dependent on risk analysis, difficult time management.

q: Which RUP phase establishes the business case for the system?
vi: Inception: business case. Elaboration: hiểu domain và kiến trúc. Construction: design, code, test. Transition: deploy.
en: Inception: business case. Elaboration: problem domain and architecture. Construction: design, programming, testing. Transition: deploy.

q: In RUP, developing an understanding of the problem domain and the system architecture happens in:
vi: Elaboration: hiểu problem domain và xây kiến trúc hệ thống.
en: Elaboration: develop an understanding of the problem domain and the system architecture.

q: Which is the correct order of RUP phases?
vi: Inception → Elaboration → Construction → Transition.
en: Inception → Elaboration → Construction → Transition.

q: In RUP, each iteration is considered:
vi: Mỗi iteration là một chu kỳ waterfall, có entry/exit criteria.
en: Each iteration is considered a waterfall cycle with entry and exit criteria.

q: Complete the Agile value: "Working software over ___".
vi: Working software over comprehensive documentation.
en: Working software over comprehensive documentation.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the four Agile values?
o: Individuals and interactions over processes and tools
Following a plan over responding to change
vi: Đúng phải là "Responding to change over following a plan". Lựa chọn này bị đảo ngược.
en: The real value is "Responding to change over following a plan"; this option reverses it.

q: The Agile Manifesto consists of:
vi: 4 giá trị nền tảng + 12 nguyên tắc.
en: 4 foundational values and 12 supporting principles.

q: The philosophy of Extreme Programming (XP) is to:
o: Take known good practices and push them to extremes
Use long iterations of several months
vi: XP: lấy các good practice đã biết và đẩy đến mức cực đoan.
en: XP takes known good practices and pushes them to extremes.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the 12 XP practices?
vi: Daily Scrum là event của Scrum, không phải XP practice.
en: Daily Scrum is a Scrum event, not an XP practice.

q: According to the Scrum Guide 2020, a Sprint lasts:
o: As long as the Product Owner decides
vi: Sprint ≤ 1 tháng (thường 2 tuần), chứa mọi event khác. "Đúng 2 tuần" là bẫy.
en: A Sprint is one month or less (commonly 2 weeks) and contains all other events.

q: The Daily Scrum is a 15-minute event for:
o: The Product Owner to report to stakeholders
The Developers to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal
The Scrum Master to assign tasks
vi: Daily Scrum: 15 phút, cho Developers kiểm tra tiến độ hướng tới Sprint Goal.
en: Daily Scrum: 15 minutes for the Developers to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal.

q: In the Scrum Guide 2020, the commitment for the Increment is:
vi: Product Backlog ↔ Product Goal; Sprint Backlog ↔ Sprint Goal; Increment ↔ Definition of Done.
en: Product Backlog ↔ Product Goal; Sprint Backlog ↔ Sprint Goal; Increment ↔ Definition of Done.

q: The Product Goal is the commitment for which artifact?
vi: Product Goal là commitment của Product Backlog.
en: The Product Goal is the commitment for the Product Backlog.

q: Which statement about burndown charts is TRUE according to the lecture?
o: They are a required Scrum artifact
They are a common practice but not required by the Scrum Guide
They are only used in Kanban
vi: Burndown chart là thói quen phổ biến, không bắt buộc theo Scrum Guide.
en: A burndown chart is a common practice, not required by the Scrum Guide.

q: According to the Scrum Guide 2020, which of the following is NOT an accountability in a Scrum Team?
vi: Chỉ có 3 trách nhiệm: PO, SM, Developers. Không có manager hay team lead trong Scrum.
en: Only three accountabilities: Product Owner, Scrum Master, Developers. No manager or team lead inside Scrum.

q: In Scrum, who orders the Product Backlog and defines the Product Goal?
vi: Product Owner: tối đa hoá giá trị, định nghĩa Product Goal, sắp thứ tự Product Backlog.
en: Product Owner: maximizes value, defines the Product Goal, orders the Product Backlog.

q: In Scrum, who coaches the team and organization and removes impediments?
vi: Scrum Master: thiết lập Scrum, coach team và tổ chức, gỡ impediments.
en: Scrum Master: establishes Scrum, coaches the team and organization, removes impediments.

q: Which of the following is NOT a Scrum event according to the lecture?
vi: Release planning là thói quen phổ biến nhưng không phải Scrum event.
en: Release planning is a common practice but not a Scrum event.

q: Which Scrum event is used to inspect how the team worked and plan improvements?
vi: Retrospective: xem lại cách team làm việc. Review: xem Increment cùng stakeholders.
en: Retrospective: inspect how the team worked. Review: inspect the Increment with stakeholders.

q: A Scrum Team is typically:
vi: Một Scrum Team thường 10 người trở xuống, tự quản.
en: One Scrum Team, typically 10 or fewer people, self-managing.

q: Kanban was introduced by whom for material production?
vi: Taiichi Ohno (Toyota) giới thiệu Kanban; David J. Anderson áp dụng cho phần mềm khoảng 2004.
en: Taiichi Ohno introduced Kanban at Toyota; David J. Anderson applied it to software around 2004.

q: Who applied Kanban to software development around 2004?
vi: David J. Anderson, khoảng năm 2004.
en: David J. Anderson, around 2004.

q: Which is a core practice of Kanban?
vi: Core practices: visualize the flow, limit WIP, dùng reports/charts (cumulative flow diagram).
en: Core practices: visualize the flow of work, limit WIP, use reports and charts (cumulative flow diagram).

q: Which chart does Kanban use to visualize progress?
vi: Kanban dùng cumulative flow diagram.
en: Kanban uses the cumulative flow diagram.

q: Which statement about Kanban is TRUE?
o: It uses fixed-length iterations like Scrum
It has no iteration like Scrum
vi: Kanban không có iteration như Scrum: xong một item thì thêm item mới.
en: Kanban has no iteration like Scrum: when an item is completed, a new item is added.

q: Which is one of Kanban's four principles?
o: Replace all current processes on day one
Respect current roles, responsibilities and job titles
vi: 4 principles: start with what you do now; incremental, evolutionary change; respect current roles; leadership at all levels.
en: Four principles: start with what you do now; incremental, evolutionary change; respect current roles; leadership at all levels.

q: Which format is used for a user story in the lecture?
o: As a [user], I want [goal], so that [benefit]
vi: User story: As a [user], I want [goal], so that [benefit]. Given/When/Then là acceptance criteria.
en: User story: As a [user], I want [goal], so that [benefit]. Given/When/Then is for acceptance criteria.

q: Which abbreviation is expanded INCORRECTLY?
vi: RUP = Rational Unified Process, không phải "Rapid". Các cách viết còn lại đều đúng.
en: RUP = Rational Unified Process, not "Rapid". The other expansions are correct.

q: In "CMMI", the final "I" stands for:
vi: CMMI = Capability Maturity Model Integration. Bẫy: CMMI dùng để process improvement và do SEI (Institute) phát triển, nhưng chữ I cuối là Integration.
en: CMMI = Capability Maturity Model Integration. Trap: CMMI is about process improvement and came from SEI (an Institute), but the final I is Integration.

q: A research project produces mainly:
vi: Production → product; Investment → benefit; Research → knowledge.
en: Production → product; Investment → benefit; Research → knowledge.

q: Which three project factors are shown in the lecture?
vi: Ba yếu tố dự án: Scope, Time, Budget.
en: The project factors are Scope, Time and Budget.

q: Which is a reason why software projects are different and hard to manage?
o: Software does not depend on people
vi: Software vô hình, linh hoạt, process linh hoạt, phụ thuộc yếu tố con người.
en: Software is intangible and flexible, processes are flexible, and projects depend on human factors.

q: Which role mainly focuses on technical quality, team capability, architecture and engineering process?
vi: Project Manager: scope, schedule, cost, risk. Engineering Manager: chất lượng kỹ thuật, năng lực team. Team Lead: điều phối kỹ thuật hằng ngày.
en: PM: scope, schedule, cost, risks. Engineering Manager: technical quality, team capability. Team Lead: daily technical coordination.

q: Which role handles daily technical coordination, task assignment and code/design support?
vi: Team Lead: điều phối kỹ thuật hằng ngày, giao task, hỗ trợ code/design.
en: Team Lead: daily technical coordination, task assignment, code/design support.

q: A feasibility report and project proposal are key outputs of which management activity?
vi: Initiation: vì sao làm dự án, có khả thi không → feasibility report, proposal.
en: Initiation: why do this project, is it feasible → feasibility report, project proposal.

q: Progress reports, issue logs and change requests are outputs of which activity?
vi: Tracking & Control: đang ở đâu, có vấn đề gì, cần đổi gì.
en: Tracking & Control: where are we, what problems occur, what should change.

q: Which statement about project planning is correct?
o: Planning is done once at the start
Planning is a continuous activity and plans are revised to reflect reality
vi: Planning liên tục từ đầu đến cuối dự án, kế hoạch được sửa theo thực tế. Agile plan theo release, sprint, ngày.
en: Planning is continuous until the project ends and plans are revised. Agile plans in release, sprint and day horizons.

q: Scope definition determines:
o: Only the features that will be delivered
What the project will and will not deliver
vi: Scope: dự án sẽ giao gì và không giao gì.
en: Scope definition determines what the project will and will not deliver.

q: According to the WBS rule of thumb, each work item should be clear enough to be:
vi: Mỗi work item trong WBS phải đủ rõ để giao, ước lượng và theo dõi.
en: Each WBS item should be clear enough to be assigned, estimated and tracked.

q: An estimation approach that uses a formula based on product size and process characteristics is:
vi: Algorithmic cost modeling: dùng công thức theo size và đặc điểm process.
en: Algorithmic cost modeling uses a formula based on product attributes like size and process characteristics.

q: Which size measure is independent of the programming language?
vi: FP đo chức năng từ góc nhìn user, độc lập ngôn ngữ. LOC phụ thuộc ngôn ngữ.
en: Function Points measure functionality from the user's perspective and are language-independent; LOC is language-dependent.

q: In the COCOMO model shown in the lecture, effort is estimated as:
vi: $\text{Effort} = a \times \text{KLOC}^{b}$; $\text{Duration} = c \times \text{Effort}^{d}$; $\text{Cost} = \text{Effort} \times$ giá/man-month.
en: $\text{Effort} = a \times \text{KLOC}^{b}$; $\text{Duration} = c \times \text{Effort}^{d}$; $\text{Cost} = \text{Effort} \times \text{cost per man-month}$.

q: How is cost estimated in the lecture?
vi: $\text{Cost} = \text{Effort} \times$ chi phí mỗi man-month.
en: $\text{Cost} = \text{Effort} \times \text{cost per man-month}$.

q: A task needs 24 person-hours. One student works 3 hours/day on it. How many days does it take?
vi: 24 / 3 = 8 ngày. Effort khác duration.
en: 24 / 3 = 8 days. Effort is not the same as duration.

q: The remaining backlog is 120 story points and the average velocity is 20 points per sprint. About how many sprints are needed?
vi: Số sprint $\approx 120 / 20 = 6$ sprint (12 tuần nếu sprint 2 tuần).
en: $\text{Sprints} \approx 120 / 20 = 6$ sprints (12 weeks with 2-week sprints).

q: Which statement about story points and velocity is correct?
o: Velocity should be used to compare different teams
Story points compare items within one team; do not compare teams by velocity
Velocity is set by the manager
vi: Story points chỉ so sánh trong một team; không so velocity giữa các team.
en: Story points compare items within one team; do not compare teams by velocity.

q: According to the lecture, adding people to a late project:
o: Makes it later because of communication overhead and extra training
vi: Thêm người vào dự án đang trễ làm nó trễ hơn (overhead giao tiếp, đào tạo thêm).
en: Adding people to a late project makes it later: communication overheads and extra training.

q: Results delivered to customers or users are called:
vi: Deliverable: kết quả giao cho khách/người dùng. Milestone: điểm kết thúc một giai đoạn.
en: Deliverables are results delivered to customers or users; milestones are end-points of a period.

q: The critical path is:
o: The longest chain of dependent tasks from start to finish
The path with the most people
The path with the highest cost
vi: Critical path là chuỗi task phụ thuộc DÀI NHẤT, quyết định thời gian tối thiểu của dự án.
en: The critical path is the LONGEST chain of dependent tasks; it determines the minimum project duration.

q: Tasks on the critical path have:
vi: $\text{Slack} = \text{latest start} - \text{earliest start}$; task găng có slack = 0.
en: $\text{Slack} = \text{latest start} - \text{earliest start}$; critical tasks have zero slack.

q: Tasks: T1 3d (none), T2 2d (T1), T3 2d (T1), T4 5d (T2, T3), T5 3d (T4), T6 1d (T5). What is the minimum project duration?
vi: T1→T2→T4→T5→T6 = 3+2+5+3+1 = 14; đường qua T3 cũng 14. Cả hai đều găng.
en: T1→T2→T4→T5→T6 = 3+2+5+3+1 = 14; the path via T3 is also 14. Both are critical.

q: In the same example (minimum 14 days), if T4 is delayed by 2 days, the project duration becomes:
vi: T4 nằm trên critical path nên trễ 2 ngày thì cả dự án trễ 2 ngày: 16.
en: T4 is on the critical path, so a 2-day delay delays the project: 16 days.

q: In the same example, if T2 is delayed by 1 day, the project duration becomes:
o: 14 days, because T3 runs in parallel
15 days, because T2 is on a critical path
vi: Cả hai đường đều găng (slack = 0), nên T2 trễ 1 ngày thì dự án thành 15 ngày.
en: Both paths are critical (zero slack), so a 1-day delay on T2 makes it 15 days.

q: What is the correct order of risk management activities?
vi: Identify → Analyze → Plan → Monitor.
en: Identification → Analysis → Planning → Monitoring.

q: Risk exposure (RE) is calculated as:
vi: $\text{RE} = \text{Probability} \times \text{Loss}$.
en: $\text{RE} = \text{Probability} \times \text{Loss}$.

q: Using the lecture's scale (Unlikely 10, Seldom 25, Occasional 50, Likely 75, Frequently 90; Catastrophic 90), what is the RE of a Likely × Catastrophic risk?
Using the lecture's scale (Occasional = 50, Serious = 75), what is the RE of an Occasional × Serious risk?
"Key staff are ill and unavailable at critical times" is which type of risk?
vi: People risk: nhân sự ốm, không tuyển được người đủ kỹ năng, thiếu đào tạo.
en: People risk: key staff ill, cannot recruit skilled staff, training unavailable.

q: "The database cannot process as many transactions per second as expected" is which type of risk?
vi: Technology risk.
en: Technology risk.

q: "The size of the software is underestimated" is which type of risk?
vi: Estimation risk: ước lượng thiếu thời gian hoặc kích thước.
en: Estimation risk: time or size underestimated.

q: In risk planning, which plans are followed when a risk actually arises?
vi: Contingency plans: kế hoạch dự phòng, dùng khi rủi ro xảy ra.
en: Contingency plans are followed if risks arise.

q: In the software risks table, "Product competition" mainly affects the:
vi: Product competition và Technology change ảnh hưởng tới Business.
en: Product competition and technology change affect the Business.

q: Which practice is recommended for risk monitoring?
o: Assess risks only at project start
Maintain a list of top-10 risks and review it regularly
vi: Đánh giá rủi ro định kỳ, giữ danh sách top-10, rủi ro ưu tiên cao báo cáo hằng tuần.
en: Assess risks regularly, maintain a top-10 list, and report high-priority risks weekly.

q: In the lecture, a risk is defined as:
o: A probability that some adverse circumstance will occur
vi: Risk là xác suất một sự cố bất lợi xảy ra.
en: A risk is a probability that some adverse circumstance will occur.

q: Which pair of abbreviations is expanded correctly?
o: WBS = Work Budget Sheet · CPM = Critical Path Method
WBS = Work Breakdown Structure · CPM = Cost Performance Metric
WBS = Weekly Build Schedule · CPM = Change Planning Model
WBS = Work Breakdown Structure · CPM = Critical Path Method
vi: WBS = Work Breakdown Structure (03#17) · CPM = Critical Path Method (03#31).
en: WBS = Work Breakdown Structure (03#17) · CPM = Critical Path Method (03#31).

q: In $\text{RE} = \text{Probability} \times \text{Loss}$, RE means:
vi: RE = Risk exposure, dùng để xếp ưu tiên rủi ro. Requirements engineering là chủ đề bài 04, không liên quan công thức này.
en: RE = Risk exposure, used to prioritize risks. Requirements engineering is lecture 04 and unrelated to this formula.

q: Which statement about LOC and FP is correct?
o: LOC = Lines of Code, language-independent; FP = Function Points, language-dependent
LOC = Lines of Code, language-dependent; FP = Function Points, language-independent
LOC = Level of Complexity, language-dependent; FP = Function Points, language-independent
LOC = Lines of Code, language-dependent; FP = Feature Priority, language-independent
vi: LOC = Lines of Code: đơn giản nhưng phụ thuộc ngôn ngữ. FP = Function Points: đo chức năng từ góc nhìn người dùng, độc lập ngôn ngữ.
en: LOC = Lines of Code: simple but language-dependent. FP = Function Points: functionality from the user's view, language-independent.

q: Requirements specify:
o: The services that a system provides and the constraints for the system
vi: Requirements = services hệ thống cung cấp + constraints.
en: Requirements specify the services a system provides and its constraints.

q: A system stakeholder is:
o: Any person or organization who is affected by the system
vi: Stakeholder: bất kỳ người hay tổ chức nào bị hệ thống ảnh hưởng.
en: Any person or organization who is affected by the system.

q: In an ATM system, the account database is an example of which viewpoint?
vi: Interactor: người hoặc hệ thống tương tác trực tiếp, gồm khách hàng VÀ account database.
en: Interactor viewpoints are people or systems interacting directly: customers AND the account database.

q: In an ATM system, management and security staff are which viewpoint?
vi: Indirect: không trực tiếp dùng hệ thống nhưng ảnh hưởng requirements.
en: Indirect viewpoints don't use the system themselves but influence the requirements.

q: Standards for inter-bank communications are an example of which viewpoint?
vi: Domain viewpoint: đặc điểm và ràng buộc của lĩnh vực.
en: Domain viewpoints are domain characteristics and constraints.

q: Which statement describes system requirements?
o: Natural-language statements from the user's point of view
A structured document detailing the system's functions, services and operational constraints
vi: User requirements: ngôn ngữ tự nhiên, góc nhìn user. System requirements: tài liệu có cấu trúc, chi tiết, góc nhìn kỹ thuật.
en: User requirements: natural language, user's view. System requirements: structured, detailed, technical view.

q: "The user shall be able to search either all of the initial set of databases or select a subset from it" is a:
vi: Đây là ví dụ functional requirement của library system trên slide.
en: This is the lecture's functional requirement example for the library system.

q: "There shall be a standard user interface to all databases which shall be based on the Z39.50 standard" is a:
vi: Ví dụ domain requirement của library system trên slide.
en: The lecture's domain requirement example for the library system.

q: Ethical, privacy and safety requirements belong to which non-functional requirement type?
vi: Product: usability, security, performance… Organizational: delivery, implementation, standards. External: ethical, privacy, safety.
en: Product: usability, security, performance. Organizational: delivery, implementation, standards. External: ethical, privacy, safety.

q: Delivery, implementation and standards requirements are which NFR type?
vi: Organizational requirements: delivery, implementation, standards.
en: Organizational requirements: delivery, implementation, standards.

q: Which is a VERIFIABLE non-functional requirement?
o: The system should be easy to use
The system should minimize user errors
Experienced controllers shall be able to use all the system functions after a total of two hours training
vi: Verifiable NFR phải có thước đo kiểm tra khách quan (2 giờ đào tạo). Các câu còn lại chỉ là goal.
en: A verifiable NFR uses a measure that can be objectively tested (two hours of training); the others are goals.

q: Which is NOT listed as a property of good functional requirements?
vi: FR tốt: precision, completeness, consistency. Portability là NFR.
en: Good FRs: precision, completeness, consistency. Portability is an NFR.

q: Which are the problems of domain requirements?
vi: Understandability: dùng ngôn ngữ của domain. Implicitness: chuyên gia domain quên nói rõ.
en: Understandability (domain language) and implicitness (experts don't make them explicit).

q: In the lecture's RE process (Feasibility study → Gathering → Specification → Validation), which activity is performed throughout the project rather than as one step in that sequence?
vi: Sơ đồ vẽ Requirements management tách riêng, vì quản lý thay đổi requirement được thực hiện xuyên suốt dự án.
en: Requirements management is drawn separately because requirements change management is performed throughout the project.

q: Requirements gathering is also called:
vi: Requirements gathering = elicitation = discovery.
en: Requirements gathering is also called elicitation or discovery.

q: In MoSCoW, "important but not vital; a workaround exists" describes:
vi: Must: thiếu là release fail. Should: quan trọng nhưng có cách lách. Could: có thì tốt. Won't: thoả thuận bỏ khỏi release này.
en: Must: release fails without it. Should: important, workaround exists. Could: nice to have. Won't: agreed to leave out this release.

q: In MoSCoW, "Won't have (this time)" means:
o: Agreed to leave out of this release
Nice to have if time allows
vi: Won't (this time): thoả thuận không làm trong release này, không phải bỏ vĩnh viễn.
en: Won't (this time): agreed to leave out of this release, not rejected forever.

q: Which gathering method has the limitation that it may interfere with the client's business?
vi: Observing: tốn thời gian của dev team và có thể làm phiền hoạt động của khách. Interview tốn thời gian khách.
en: Observing costs the development team's time and may interfere with the client's business. Interviews cost the client's time.

q: Which gathering technique reaches many users quickly and is good for quantitative data?
vi: Questionnaires/surveys: tiếp cận nhiều người nhanh, hợp dữ liệu định lượng.
en: Questionnaires and surveys reach many users quickly and suit quantitative data.

q: A software requirements document should state:
o: HOW the system should do it
WHAT the system should do rather than HOW
vi: SRS nêu WHAT, không phải HOW.
en: The SRS states WHAT the system should do rather than HOW.

q: IEEE 830 (1998) has been replaced by:
vi: IEEE 830 → ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018.
en: IEEE 830 was replaced by ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018.

q: In the INVEST criteria for user stories, "E" stands for:
vi: INVEST: Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable.
en: INVEST: Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable.

q: Acceptance criteria in the lecture are written in which format, and what do they become?
o: As a/I want/so that; they become epics
Given/When/Then; they become acceptance test cases
vi: Acceptance criteria viết dạng Given/When/Then và trở thành acceptance test cases.
en: Acceptance criteria use Given/When/Then and become acceptance test cases.

q: "Can the requirements be implemented given available budget and technology?" is which requirements check?
vi: Realism: có làm được với ngân sách và công nghệ hiện có không.
en: Realism: can they be implemented with the available budget and technology.

q: "Are there any requirements conflicts?" is which requirements check?
vi: Consistency: có mâu thuẫn giữa các requirement không.
en: Consistency: are there any requirement conflicts.

q: "Does the system provide the functions which best support the customer's needs?" is which check?
vi: Validity: chức năng có hỗ trợ tốt nhất nhu cầu khách không.
en: Validity: does the system provide the functions that best support the customer's needs.

q: Which requirements validation technique is the most common approach?
vi: Requirements reviews: phân tích thủ công có hệ thống, phổ biến nhất.
en: Requirements reviews (systematic manual analysis) are the most common approach.

q: Developing tests for requirements to check their testability is called:
vi: Test-case generation: viết test cho requirement để kiểm tra tính testable.
en: Test-case generation: developing tests for requirements to check testability.

q: What are the main steps of requirements change management?
o: Change request → Change analysis and costing → Change implementation
vi: Change request → change analysis & costing → change implementation.
en: Change request → change analysis and costing → change implementation.

q: A requirements traceability matrix is used for:
o: Impact analysis when requirements change and checking test coverage
vi: Traceability: liên kết requirement ↔ nguồn, design, test → impact analysis và kiểm tra test coverage.
en: Traceability links requirements to sources, design and tests: used for impact analysis and test coverage.

q: In RUP, the two main types of requirements documents are:
vi: RUP: Vision document + use-case specs. Agile (Scrum, XP): Vision + user stories.
en: RUP: Vision document and use-case specifications. Agile: vision and user stories.

q: What is a key risk of AI-assisted requirements engineering mentioned in the lecture?
o: AI does not know your stakeholders and can invent plausible requirements
AI always refuses to write user stories
vi: AI không biết stakeholder của bạn, có thể bịa requirement nghe hợp lý → luôn validate với user thật.
en: AI does not know your stakeholders and can invent plausible requirements; always validate with real users.

q: Which abbreviation is expanded INCORRECTLY?
o: MoSCoW = Must / Should / Could / Won't have (this time)
INVEST = Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable
vi: SRS = Software Requirements Specification. Các cách viết còn lại đều đúng.
en: SRS = Software Requirements Specification. The other expansions are correct.

q: "Mean time to failure" (MTTF) is a measure for which non-functional property?
vi: Reliability đo bằng MTTF, xác suất không sẵn sàng, tần suất lỗi, availability. Bẫy: Robustness đo bằng thời gian khởi động lại sau lỗi.
en: Reliability: MTTF, probability of unavailability, rate of failure, availability. Trap: robustness is measured by time to restart after failure.

q: UML was created by unifying the work of:
vi: Grady Booch, James Rumbaugh, Ivar Jacobson (Rational Software).
en: Grady Booch, James Rumbaugh and Ivar Jacobson of Rational Software.

q: UML was adopted as a standard by the Object Management Group (OMG) in:
vi: OMG chuẩn hoá UML năm 1997.
en: OMG adopted UML as a standard in 1997.

q: A use case diagram belongs to which UML group?
vi: Use case diagram thuộc nhóm behavioral (dynamic), cùng sequence, communication, state machine, activity.
en: Use case diagrams are behavioral (dynamic), with sequence, communication, state machine and activity diagrams.

q: Which of the following is a structural UML diagram?
vi: Structural: class, package, object, component, deployment.
en: Structural: class, package, object, component, deployment.

q: Which statement about actors is correct?
o: One physical user can play only one actor
An actor represents a role; one physical user can play multiple roles
Actors are internal classes of the system
vi: Actor là một role; một người thật có thể đóng nhiều role; nhiều người cùng role là một actor; actor có thể là process hoặc hệ thống.
en: An actor is a role; one user can play several roles; many users with the same role are one actor; actors can be processes or things.

q: A use case specifies:
o: HOW the system does something internally
WHAT the system does, but not HOW
vi: Use case nêu WHAT, không HOW; che giấu cấu trúc bên trong.
en: A use case specifies WHAT the system does, not HOW; it hides internal structure.

q: A use case description has:
o: One main (basic) flow and alternative flows
vi: Một basic flow + alternative flows (alternative, exceptional paths).
en: One main (basic) flow plus alternative flows (alternative and exceptional paths).

q: A scenario is:
o: An instance of a use case: a specific sequence of events
vi: Scenario là một instance cụ thể của use case (giống object so với class).
en: A scenario is a specific sequence of events, an instance of a use case (like object vs class).

q: Which statement about the INCLUDE relationship is correct?
o: The included use case may stand alone
The base use case is not aware of the included use case
The base use case is aware of its included use case, and the included use case does not stand alone
Include is between an actor and a use case
vi: Include: base BIẾT use case được include; use case được include không đứng một mình.
en: Include: the base is aware of the included use case; the included use case does not stand alone.

q: Which statement about the EXTEND relationship is correct?
o: The base use case is aware of the extending use case
The extending use case may stand alone and the base is not aware of it
The extending use case cannot stand alone
vi: Extend: base KHÔNG biết use case mở rộng; use case mở rộng có thể đứng một mình.
en: Extend: the base is not aware of the extending use case; the extending use case may stand alone.

q: In the online shopping example, the <<extend>> arrow is drawn:
o: From Checkout order to Verify shipping address
From Verify shipping address to Checkout order
From Customer to Verify shipping address
vi: Mũi tên extend đi từ use case mở rộng (Verify shipping address) về base (Checkout order).
en: The extend arrow goes from the extending use case (Verify shipping address) to the base (Checkout order).

q: In the online shopping example, what is the relationship from "Checkout order" to "Payment"?
vi: Checkout order <<include>> Payment: thanh toán là phần bắt buộc của checkout.
en: Checkout order <<include>> Payment: payment is an explicit part of checkout.

q: In the Firefox example, "Read web page loud" relates to "Load and Display web page" by:
vi: Read web page loud <<extend>> Load and Display web page (tuỳ chọn, base không biết).
en: Read web page loud <<extend>> Load and Display web page (optional; the base is not aware).

q: According to the notes on use case diagrams, a well-defined use case should:
o: Put all variations into the base use case
Include common behavior from included use cases and distribute variations into extending use cases
Contain every actor of the system
vi: Hành vi chung → include; biến thể → extend.
en: Common behavior goes into included use cases; variations into extending use cases.

q: Which statement correctly contrasts UI and UX?
o: UI covers the user's overall experience; UX is the look and feel
UI refers to the interactivity, look and feel of a screen; UX covers the user's overall experience with the product
vi: UI: tương tác, look & feel của màn hình. UX: toàn bộ trải nghiệm với sản phẩm.
en: UI: interactivity, look and feel of a screen. UX: the user's overall experience with the product.

q: According to the lecture, short-term memory can hold about how many chunks at a time?
vi: Khoảng 4 ± 1 chunk; ước lượng kinh điển của Miller là 7 ± 2.
en: About 4 ± 1 chunks; Miller's classic estimate is 7 ± 2.

q: "Comparable operations should be activated in the same way" is which UI design principle?
vi: Consistency: các thao tác tương tự được kích hoạt giống nhau.
en: Consistency: comparable operations are activated in the same way.

q: "Users should never be surprised by the behavior of a system" is which principle?
vi: Minimal surprise.
en: Minimal surprise.

q: "The interface should include mechanisms to allow users to recover from errors" is which principle?
vi: Recoverability: có cơ chế để người dùng khôi phục sau lỗi.
en: Recoverability: mechanisms to let users recover from errors.

q: "The interface should use terms and concepts drawn from the experience of the people who will make most use of the system" is:
vi: User familiarity: dùng thuật ngữ quen thuộc với người dùng.
en: User familiarity: use terms and concepts familiar to the main users.

q: "Provide meaningful feedback when errors occur and context-sensitive help" is which principle?
vi: User guidance: feedback có ý nghĩa khi lỗi và trợ giúp theo ngữ cảnh.
en: User guidance: meaningful feedback on errors and context-sensitive help.

q: In WCAG 2.2, a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 for text belongs to which POUR principle?
vi: Perceivable: alt text, phụ đề, tương phản ≥ 4.5:1.
en: Perceivable: text alternatives, captions, contrast ratio ≥ 4.5:1 for text.

q: "Everything works with a keyboard; targets large enough to tap" belongs to which POUR principle?
vi: Operable: dùng được bằng bàn phím, vùng bấm đủ lớn.
en: Operable: everything works with a keyboard; targets large enough to tap.

q: Which accessibility rule is stated in the lecture?
o: Use color alone to signal errors
Never use color alone to convey meaning
vi: Không bao giờ dùng mỗi màu sắc để truyền ý nghĩa.
en: Never use color alone to convey meaning.

q: Which interaction style requires users to learn syntax and options?
vi: Command language: phải học cú pháp và tuỳ chọn.
en: Command language: users must learn syntax and options.

q: Which interaction style is used when data entry is required?
vi: Form fill-in: dùng khi cần nhập dữ liệu.
en: Form fill-in is used when data entry is required.

q: Which interaction style lets users directly make changes and see results?
vi: Direct manipulation: thay đổi trực tiếp và thấy kết quả.
en: Direct manipulation: users directly make changes and see results.

q: Digital presentation of information is best for:
o: Precise values using little screen space
vi: Digital: giá trị chính xác, ít chỗ. Analogue: thể hiện giá trị tương đối.
en: Digital: precise values, little screen space. Analogue: relative values.

q: What is the order of the UI design process in the lecture?
o: System prototyping → User analysis → Interface evaluation
User analysis → System prototyping → Interface evaluation
Interface evaluation → User analysis → System prototyping
User analysis → Interface evaluation → System prototyping
vi: User analysis → System prototyping → Interface evaluation.
en: User analysis → System prototyping → Interface evaluation.

q: Which user analysis technique observes the user at work?
vi: Ethnography: quan sát người dùng khi làm việc.
en: Ethnography observes the user at work.

q: System prototyping is described as a two-stage process of:
vi: Hai giai đoạn: paper prototypes → automated prototypes.
en: Two stages: paper prototypes, then automated prototypes.

q: According to the lecture, error messages should be:
vi: Thông báo lỗi: polite, concise, consistent, constructive; dựa trên nền tảng và kinh nghiệm người dùng.
en: Messages should be polite, concise, consistent and constructive, based on users' background and experience.

q: Which is NOT one of the usability attributes used in interface evaluation?
vi: Usability attributes: learnability, speed of operation, robustness, recoverability, adaptability.
en: Usability attributes: learnability, speed of operation, robustness, recoverability, adaptability.

q: Which is listed as a common mistake in using color in interface design?
o: Using color change to show status change
vi: Sai lầm thường gặp: dùng màu để truyền ý nghĩa và lạm dụng màu.
en: Common mistakes: using color to communicate meaning and over-using color.

q: Which principle of data validation does the lecture state?
o: Trust user input to save time
Do not trust the users; check all user input data
Validate only on the server once a day
vi: Không tin người dùng, kiểm tra mọi dữ liệu nhập; ràng buộc natural/business; early hoặc late checking.
en: Do not trust the users; check all input; natural and business constraints; early or late checking.

q: Which abbreviation is expanded INCORRECTLY?
o: BPMN = Business Process Model and Notation
vi: UML = Unified Modeling Language, không phải "Universal". Các cách viết còn lại đều đúng.
en: UML = Unified Modeling Language, not "Universal". The other expansions are correct.

q: In WCAG 2.2, the "R" in POUR stands for:
vi: POUR = Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, Robust. Robust: HTML ngữ nghĩa, chạy được với screen reader. Bẫy: slide cũng nói thiết kế responsive, nhưng đó không phải chữ R.
en: POUR = Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, Robust. Robust: semantic HTML, works with screen readers. Trap: the slide also says design responsive, but that is not the R.

q: In the software development process on the slide, architectural design belongs to which step?
vi: Thiết kế nằm ở bước Analysis & Design, sau Requirement definition.
en: Design sits in the Analysis & Design step.

q: Software design is best defined as:
o: Writing and testing the source code
Conceptualizing how a system will work before it is implemented or modified
vi: Software design: hình dung hệ thống hoạt động thế nào trước khi cài đặt hoặc sửa.
en: Conceptualizing how the system will work before implementing or modifying it.

q: On the slide, architectural design is the level of software design that covers:
o: The overall structure of the system
The test cases for each module
vi: Architectural design: cấu trúc tổng thể. High-level: sub-system và module. Detailed: cấu trúc dữ liệu và thuật toán.
en: Architectural design: overall structure. High-level: sub-systems and modules. Detailed: data structures and algorithms.

q: Which is NOT part of architectural design?
o: Identifying major components and their communications
Making design decisions and their rationale
Choosing the sorting algorithm inside one function
vi: Thuật toán bên trong một hàm thuộc detailed design.
en: Algorithms inside a function belong to detailed design.

q: "The set of structures needed to reason about the system, comprising software elements, relations among them, and properties of both" is the definition by:
vi: Định nghĩa này của Bass, Clements & Kazman (Software Architecture in Practice, 4th ed., 2021). Shaw et al. nói về components và interactions.
en: That is Bass, Clements & Kazman (2021); Shaw et al. speak of components and interactions.

q: Who created the C4 model?
vi: C4 model của Simon Brown, bốn mức phóng to như bản đồ.
en: The C4 model is by Simon Brown.

q: For the course project (PA3), which C4 diagrams should you draw at least?
o: All four, with full UML for each
vi: Đồ án: ít nhất System Context và Container diagram (PA3).
en: At least the Context and Container diagrams (PA3).

q: Which tools are listed for diagrams-as-code in C4?
vi: Diagrams-as-code: Structurizr, PlantUML, Mermaid.
en: Structurizr, PlantUML, Mermaid.

q: A module (component), unlike a sub-system:
o: Is a system in its own right
Provides services to other components but is not normally a separate system
Must run on its own server
vi: Module cung cấp dịch vụ cho component khác nhưng thường không được xem là hệ thống riêng.
en: A module serves other components but is not normally a separate system.

q: "Analysis of whether the system can meet its non-functional requirements" is which advantage of architecture?
vi: System analysis: kiểm tra NFR và khả năng mở rộng sau này.
en: System analysis covers NFRs and future extensions.

q: To improve availability, the architecture should:
o: Include redundant components and fault-tolerance mechanisms
Put critical assets in inner layers
Localize safety features in few sub-systems
vi: Availability: thêm component dự phòng và cơ chế chịu lỗi.
en: Availability: redundant components and fault tolerance.

q: Which architectural choice supports maintainability?
vi: Maintainability: component nhỏ, dễ thay. Large-grain là cho performance.
en: Maintainability: fine-grain, replaceable components. Large-grain is for performance.

q: Introducing redundant data improves availability but makes which attribute harder?
vi: Conflict: dữ liệu dư thừa giúp availability nhưng làm security khó hơn.
en: Redundant data helps availability but makes security harder.

q: Localizing safety-related features usually leads to:
vi: Gom tính năng safety thường cần giao tiếp nhiều hơn, nên performance giảm.
en: It usually means more communication, so performance degrades.

q: "The system should achieve 99.99% uptime" is an architecturally significant requirement about:
vi: Uptime 99,99% là availability. 1.000 giao dịch/giây là performance; 1 triệu người dùng là scalability; ISO 27001 là security.
en: Uptime is availability; 1,000 TPS is performance; 1M users is scalability; ISO 27001 is security.

q: Data residency laws affecting a cloud architecture are an example of an ASR:
vi: Ví dụ trên slide: luật nơi lưu dữ liệu là ràng buộc (constraint) cho thiết kế.
en: The slide gives data residency laws as a design constraint.

q: Which is a high-priority functional requirement example that shapes the architecture?
o: The system must comply with ISO/IEC 27001:2022
A real-time video processing application requires a low-latency streaming pipeline
The system must handle 1,000 transactions per second
vi: Ví dụ FR ưu tiên cao: xử lý video thời gian thực cần pipeline streaming độ trễ thấp. Ba ý còn lại là NFR.
en: Real-time video needing a low-latency pipeline is the FR example; the others are NFRs.

q: Which is NOT one of the questions for architectural design?
o: How will the system be distributed?
What control strategy should be used?
How should the architecture be documented?
How many testers should the team hire?
vi: 7 câu hỏi về kiến trúc không gồm việc tuyển tester.
en: Hiring testers is not among the seven questions.

q: Which is listed as an example of a design decision?
o: Write the user manual in English
Hold a sprint review every two weeks
vi: Ví dụ quyết định thiết kế: React, React Native, MySQL, MVC phía server, Java back end, daily backup.
en: Examples: React, React Native, MySQL, MVC, Java back end, daily backup.

q: In the three-tier example decision, which were listed as alternatives?
vi: Alternatives: MVC, service-oriented architecture, n-tier.
en: Alternatives: MVC, SOA, n-tier.

q: Where is an ADR kept?
o: Only in the project manager's email
vi: ADR là tài liệu ngắn lưu ngay trong repository (docs/adr/), được review như code.
en: ADRs live in the repository (docs/adr/) and are reviewed like code.

q: Which ADR section records "benefits, drawbacks, follow-up work"?
vi: Consequences: lợi ích, hạn chế, việc tiếp theo. Context: vấn đề và ràng buộc.
en: Consequences hold benefits, drawbacks and follow-up work.

q: MVC, n-tier and service-oriented are examples of:
vi: Ví dụ architectural style trên slide: MVC, n-tier, service-oriented.
en: The slide lists them as architectural styles.

q: The repository style is often used when:
o: A fast response to hardware events is essential
Every node must act as a server
Data must pass through a series of transformations
vi: Repository hay dùng khi chia sẻ lượng dữ liệu lớn.
en: Repository is used when sharing large amounts of data.

q: Which is an ADVANTAGE of the client-server style?
o: A shared data model across sub-systems
A central register of names and services
It is easy to add new servers or upgrade existing ones
vi: Client-server dễ thêm hoặc nâng cấp server. Không có data model chung và không có registry trung tâm là nhược điểm.
en: Easy to add or upgrade servers; no shared model and no central register are drawbacks.

q: Which are given as examples of peer-to-peer systems?
vi: Ví dụ P2P: BitTorrent, mạng blockchain, một số hệ thống giao tiếp thời gian thực.
en: BitTorrent, blockchain networks, some real-time communication systems.

q: Which is an advantage of the layered style?
o: Very fast communication through all layers
vi: Layered: separation of concerns, reuse, giảm ảnh hưởng khi đổi UI.
en: Separation of concerns, reuse, less impact of UI changes.

q: MVC was originally introduced for:
vi: MVC ban đầu cho ứng dụng có giao diện, nay phổ biến cho web app.
en: Originally for UI apps, now popular for web apps.

q: In MVC, the View is responsible for:
vi: View: trình bày. Model: dữ liệu và logic. Controller: nhận lệnh.
en: View: presentation.

q: In pipes and filters, data travels between filters via:
vi: Filter xử lý độc lập, dữ liệu đi qua filter bằng pipe.
en: Data travels through filters via pipes.

q: In the interrupt-driven style, each interrupt type is associated with:
o: A memory location and a hardware switch
vi: Mỗi loại interrupt gắn với một vị trí bộ nhớ và một công tắc phần cứng, có handler riêng.
en: Each type has a memory location, a hardware switch and its own handler.

q: Autonomy, resilience, scalability and flexibility are traits of:
vi: Bộ này là của microservices. SOA: modularity, interoperability, reusability, loose coupling.
en: These are microservice traits; SOA's are modularity, interoperability, reusability, loose coupling.

q: Which is NOT a drawback of microservices listed in the lecture?
vi: Microservices mở rộng độc lập được; nhược điểm là phức tạp phân tán, nhất quán dữ liệu, chi phí vận hành, cần DevOps.
en: Independent scaling is a benefit; drawbacks are complexity, consistency, overhead, DevOps maturity.

q: In event-driven architecture, "TicketBooked" is consumed by payment, email and analytics. What sits between the producer and consumers?
o: An event broker such as Kafka or RabbitMQ
vi: Producer → event broker (Kafka, RabbitMQ) → một hoặc nhiều consumer.
en: Producer → event broker (Kafka, RabbitMQ) → consumers.

q: Which is an advantage of event-driven architecture?
o: No need to version event schemas
vi: Ưu điểm: loose coupling, dễ thêm consumer, bất đồng bộ. Nhược: khó debug, eventual consistency.
en: Loose coupling, easy to add consumers, asynchronous.

q: Which is NOT one of the main elements of a class diagram on the slide?
vi: Class diagram: classes, interfaces, relationships, common mechanisms. Lifeline thuộc sequence diagram.
en: Lifelines belong to sequence diagrams.

q: A class defines:
o: The set of objects that share the same attributes, operations, relationships and semantics
Only the data stored in a table
A step in a use case
vi: Class: tập các object có chung attribute, operation, relationship và ngữ nghĩa.
en: The set of objects sharing attributes, operations, relationships and semantics.

q: A class name must be:
o: The same as the table name
vi: Tên class phải duy nhất trong nhóm của nó.
en: Unique within its group.

q: An operation is:
o: A service that can be requested from objects of the class
A stored row in a table
vi: Operation: dịch vụ có thể yêu cầu từ các object của class. Attribute: dữ liệu mô tả class.
en: An operation is a requestable service; an attribute is characterizing data.

q: In "-cases: int", the minus sign means the attribute is:
vi: - là private, + là public, # là protected.
en: - private, + public, # protected.

q: Which relationship is described as the least restrictive?
vi: Dependency lỏng nhất trong các quan hệ.
en: Dependency is less restrictive than the others.

q: Which notation shows generalization?
o: A dashed line with an open arrow
A solid line with a hollow triangle pointing at the superclass
A filled diamond at the owner
vi: Generalization: mũi tên tam giác rỗng chỉ vào superclass.
en: A hollow triangle pointing at the superclass.

q: An association can have:
o: A name and roles at both ends
vi: Association có thể có tên và role ở hai đầu.
en: A name and roles at both ends.

q: Multiplicity refers to:
o: How many attributes a class has
How many objects may be connected across an instance of an association
How many subclasses a class has
How many times a message is sent
vi: Multiplicity: số object có thể nối qua một association.
en: How many objects may be connected across an association.

q: A Faculty uses Lecturers but does not own them. Which relationship and symbol?
vi: Aggregation: dùng nhưng không sở hữu, thoi rỗng. Composition mới là thoi đặc.
en: Aggregation: using without owning, hollow diamond.

q: In the Online Shop class diagram, "line item" is an example of:
vi: line item là role name ở đầu OrderDetail.
en: "line item" is a role name.

q: In the Online Shop diagram, the arrow from OrderDetail to Item shows:
vi: Mũi tên trên association thể hiện navigability.
en: The arrow on the association shows navigability.

q: A system object, as opposed to a domain object:
o: Is created to support processing and calculations
Takes a role in the business process
vi: System object được tạo ra để hỗ trợ xử lý và tính toán.
en: System objects support processing and calculations.

q: Screens, forms and API endpoints are which kind of BCE object?
vi: Boundary: giao diện giữa actor và hệ thống: màn hình, form, API endpoint.
en: Boundary objects: screens, forms, API endpoints.

q: Which BCE objects are domain objects?
vi: Boundary và control là system object; entity là domain object.
en: Entities are domain objects; boundary and control are system objects.

q: BCE maps to a layered architecture as:
vi: BCE khớp với presentation → business → data.
en: It maps to presentation → business → data.

q: When identifying domain classes, which should be removed?
o: Classes that play a role in the business process
vi: Bỏ class trùng, từ mơ hồ, và attribute đội lốt class.
en: Remove duplicates, vague words and attributes disguised as classes.

q: In the Shipping System example, Vessel, Region and Captain are classified as:
vi: Các entity trong domain model (Vessel, VesselType, Region, Crew, Captain) là domain object.
en: They are domain objects from the domain model.

q: In a sequence diagram, what does an activation bar show?
vi: Activation bar: khoảng thời gian object đang thực thi.
en: When an object is executing.

q: Which combined fragment means a simple "if" with no else?
vi: opt = if; alt = if/else.
en: opt = if; alt = if/else.

q: How many sequence diagrams should you draw?
o: Exactly one for the whole system
vi: Mỗi scenario quan trọng một sơ đồ.
en: One diagram per important scenario.

q: In "Register for a course", which object answers hasFreeSeat()?
vi: Controller hỏi Course hasFreeSeat(); còn chỗ thì tạo Enrollment.
en: The controller asks Course hasFreeSeat(); if a seat is free it creates an Enrollment.

q: Encapsulation (the black-box rule) means:
vi: Encapsulation: giấu dữ liệu, chỉ lộ operation.
en: Hide data, expose operations.

q: Shared data and behaviour between classes should be modelled with:
vi: Dữ liệu và hành vi dùng chung → inheritance.
en: Shared data and behaviour → inheritance.

q: Which objects need a state machine diagram?
o: Objects with a status field, such as order, booking or account
vi: Object có trường trạng thái (order, booking, account) thì vẽ state machine.
en: Objects with a status field.

q: In the Order state machine, a Paid order can be cancelled:
o: At any time, even after delivery
vi: Paid —cancel [before shipping] / refund→ Cancelled.
en: Paid → Cancelled on cancel [before shipping] / refund.

q: How does a state machine refine the class diagram?
o: Each event becomes an operation of the class
Each state becomes a new class
vi: Mỗi event → một operation: pay(), ship(), deliver(), cancel().
en: Each event becomes an operation: pay(), ship(), deliver(), cancel().

q: Coupling measures:
o: How closely responsibilities inside one module belong together
How strongly one module depends on others
How many lines of code a module has
vi: Coupling: mức phụ thuộc giữa các module. Cohesion: độ gắn bó bên trong một module.
en: Coupling is dependence between modules; cohesion is togetherness inside one.

q: What does DRY stand for?
vi: DRY = Don't Repeat Yourself.
en: DRY = Don't Repeat Yourself.

q: "Adding a new type means editing a big switch" is a symptom of violating:
vi: O: mở để mở rộng, đóng để sửa đổi.
en: Open/Closed: open for extension, closed for modification.

q: A subclass that throws "not supported" violates:
vi: L: subtype phải thay được cho base type.
en: Liskov: subtypes must be able to replace their base type.

q: Classes forced to implement empty methods suggest a violation of:
vi: I: nhiều interface nhỏ tốt hơn một interface lớn.
en: Interface Segregation: many small interfaces over one large one.

q: Observer, Strategy and State belong to which group of GoF patterns?
vi: Behavioral: Chain of Responsibility, Command, Iterator, Mediator, Observer, State, Strategy, Template Method…
en: They are behavioral patterns.

q: Builder and Prototype belong to which group?
vi: Creational: Factory Method, Abstract Factory, Builder, Prototype, Singleton.
en: Creational patterns.

q: Create the right payment method object (card, e-wallet, bank transfer). Which pattern?
vi: Tạo đúng loại object → Factory Method.
en: Creating the right object → Factory Method.

q: A simple entry point to a complex subsystem is provided by:
vi: Facade: một lối vào đơn giản cho subsystem phức tạp.
en: Facade.

q: According to the lecture, design patterns are:
o: A goal: use as many as possible
A vocabulary, applied only when the problem appears
vi: Pattern là từ vựng, không phải mục tiêu: chỉ dùng khi bài toán xuất hiện.
en: Patterns are a vocabulary, not a goal.

q: In the Strategy example, which element holds a PricingStrategy and calls calculate()?
vi: Booking giữ một PricingStrategy và gọi calculate(); các class Pricing cài interface.
en: Booking holds a PricingStrategy and calls calculate().

q: NoSQL storage (document, key-value, graph) is suggested for:
vi: NoSQL cho schema linh hoạt hoặc quy mô cực lớn.
en: Flexible schemas or massive scale.

q: How is an n – n association between Student and Course mapped?
vi: n–n: junction table có hai foreign key.
en: n–n: a junction table with two foreign keys.

q: Where do attributes of a link (association class), such as grade and date, go?
o: Extra columns in the junction table
vi: Attribute của liên kết → cột thêm trong junction table: enrollment.grade, enrollment.date.
en: Extra columns in the junction table.

q: Which is NOT an option for mapping generalization to tables?
vi: Generalization: một bảng cho cả cây, mỗi class một bảng, hoặc mỗi class cụ thể một bảng.
en: Per hierarchy, per class, or per concrete class.

q: For a database, a data specification describes:
vi: Database: mô tả các trường của bảng. File system: mô tả định dạng file.
en: Database: table fields. File system: file format.

q: Which belongs to the relational database design checklist?
o: Manage schema changes with migration scripts in Git
Store passwords in plain text for recovery
Avoid primary keys to save space
vi: Checklist: PK/FK, 3NF, kiểu dữ liệu và ràng buộc, index, đặt tên nhất quán, hash mật khẩu, migration trong Git.
en: PK/FK, 3NF, types and constraints, indexes, naming, hashed passwords, migrations in Git.
